text:
Jamie Benn walks into this one a single point from 1,000 in his career, every one of them in a Stars sweater. That's the night in Dallas, even with the noise around Jason Robertson, whose name has been all over trade-rumor headlines this week, including a Yahoo Sports piece on an insider floating a Nikita Kucherov swap. Robertson runs the top power play and carries a 36% chance to score in our numbers.

Buffalo comes in with a goaltending question it is still answering. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled in Wednesday's 8-3 loss to Tampa Bay, Alex Lyon made his season debut a night later in an overtime loss in Chicago, and Lyon is confirmed again tonight. He was 12 goals better than expected last season. The Sabres are winless in three, and Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic wrote that the bigger issue in Chicago was letting it get to overtime at all. Our numbers are kinder than the standings: a -12 goal difference on almost even expected goals, with finishing (6.5 goals below what their chances usually produce) and goaltending (5.1 goals allowed above expected) both costing them. Their playoff chance sits at 26%.

Dallas is coming off its own bad night, an 8-3 home loss to Winnipeg in which the Jets came back from two down. Miro Heiskanen is still out with an upper-body injury (ESPN estimates Nov 17), so Thomas Harley has moved onto the first power-play unit and Tyler Myers is up to 20:30 a night. Jake Oettinger, confirmed, has had a rough five starts (.842, 4.3 goals worse than expected) but is still five goals above expected on the season. The Stars sit at 77% to make the playoffs.

The matchup to watch is special teams: the Dallas power play makes 0.79 expected goals a game, Buffalo's penalty kill allows 0.77, and the Sabres take 4.1 penalties a game. Tage Thompson, scoring again lately, is one assist from 200, and Wyatt Johnston has no goals in five games on 3.0 expected. We have no sleeper picks in this game.
headline: Jamie Benn sits one point from 1,000
